pages.text: Mom from the mill took the blue neck scarf from the yard line. "Mumu, shall you tie it yourself today?" Little brother Mumu clenched both wings. "Me! I'll do it!" He wanted to tie it alone, like his sister.
Mumu draped it around his neck, but—huh? One end was long, one short. Pull the long end, and the short end slipped out. "Ooh, it won't work!" Holding the ends in his wings, he wriggled.
Mumu dropped onto the yard dirt. The blue scarf lay by his feet. "I can't even tie my scarf..." His beak drooped. He wanted to do it alone like his sister, but the slipping scarf upset him.
Mom sat beside Mumu. "This isn't a scarf. It's a little waterwheel. Once around your neck, like a wheel, then pull both ends, and done!" She showed one turn around his neck.
Big sister Dodo ran into the yard. "Round once, then pull!" Mumu spread his wings forward. "Just turn and pull?" Suddenly, scarf-tying felt like a fun game.
First, one waterwheel turn! Mumu draped the scarf and turned it around. Both ends met at the front. "They met!" He smiled. Only one turn, so it wasn't hard.
Second, pull! Mumu put one end under the other, then pulled with both wings. One little knot appeared. Mom and Dodo called together, "Round once, then pull!"
Last, tap the knot straight! The blue scarf sat snugly around his neck. All tied by himself! One tail flick. "I did it!"
Now Mumu knew the order. "One, around my neck, one turn! Two, under and pull! Three, tap the knot!" Next morning, he tied it alone before Mom even came.
Mom lifted Mumu high and rubbed cheek to cheek. "All tied by yourself!" A neck scarf is a little waterwheel turning once. Mumu tapped the knot and called, "Round once, then pull!"
